content.title: Here’s Good News For Fans Wanting A ‘Paradise’ Season 3
content.text: Sterling K. Brown in "Paradise" Season 2Disney/Paradise, starring Sterling K. Brown, James Marsden and Julianne Nicholson, released its eighth and final episode for its second season on Monday on a cliffhanger.A post-apocalyptic sci-fi series created by Dan Fogelman (This is Us), Paradise premiered on Hulu on Jan. 26, 2025, with Season 1, which consisted of eight episodes. The series returned with the first three of its eight-episode second season on Feb. 23.Note: Spoilers for Paraadise Seasons 1 and 2 are revealed throughout the rest of this article.ForbesJames Cameron’s ‘Avatar: Fire And Ash’ Is New On Streaming This WeekBy Tim LammersParadise Season 1 find U.S. Secret Service Agent Xavier Brooks (Brown) investigating the mysterious death of former U.S. President Cal Brooks (Marsden) in Paradise — a massive city-sized bunker built completely under a Colorado mountain. Paradise was constructed to keep part of humanity intact after a super volcano set off a catastrophic chain of events including a monstrous tsunamis and nuclear conflicts all around the globe.At the end of Season 1, Xavier, upon discovering who killed the president, also learns from Paradise’s most powerful leader Sinatra (Nicholson) that people survived the apocalyptic events of what is called “The Day” three years earlier, including his wife, Teri (Enuka Okuma).While Season 1 of Paradise largely took place within the underground city, Season 2 – which is streaming on Hulu on Disney+ — examines life outside for the survivors of The Day and how they are thriving. Xavier, meanwhile, is headed to Atlanta where he believes he will find Teri alive. MORE FOR YOUForbesWhy Rachel From ‘Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen’ Looks FamiliarBy Tim LammersParadise Season 2 also introduces the characters Annie (Shailene Woodley), a resourceful Graceland tour guide in Memphis who survives The Day in a bunker deep within Elvis Presley’s former abode; and Link (Thomas Doherty), the leader of a group of survivors intent on finding Paradise in Colorado to exact revenge in a storyline that develops throughout the season. Email Address Paradise Season 2 — without revealing too many major spoilers — ends with a mass exodus from the underground city and Xavier being tasked to locate a quantum supercomputer powered by artificial intelligence that has the power to manipulate time. As such, the AI supercomputer may help find a way to avert the disaster that befell Paradise in the Season 2 finale.Given that the conclusion of Paradise Season 2 leaves the door wide open for the series to continue, fans of the series will be happy to know that Paradise Season 3 is on the way.Forbes‘Paradise’ Season 2 Finale Explained: Alex Becomes Xavier’s MissionBy Sabrina Reed“In my initial pitch, I told people, ‘The second season is going to end with the bunker failing and the collapse of the whole infrastructure,’” Fogelman told the Los Angeles Times on Monday. “That was a lot to figure out: How are we going to pull that off? How is that going to send us forward into the third season? It was big and daunting.”‘Paradise’ Was Renewed For Season 3 In Mid-MarchWhile the creators of most series must await the news of whether their show will be renewed as viewership numbers are examine, Dan Fogelman received the good news on March 17 that Paradise got the green light for Season 3.News of the renewal in mid-March came with some impressive viewership statistics, according to Deadline. Not only did the new season two weeks before its finale already amass up 30 million viewing hours, Paradise Season 1 also logged an additional 25 million viewing hours.Forbes‘Scream 7’ Is New On Streaming This WeekBy Tim LammersFogelman told the LA Times that he doesn’t have plans beyond Paradise Season 3 because three seasons is all he’s ever planned for the show. Asked by the LA Times how he will react if there’s pressure to produce more seasons of Paradise beyond Season 3, Fogelman responded, “There is always pressure. But I try to resist the pressure because I think it’s the right way to tell the story. Sterling feels similarly. I was very clear from the beginning that I had a three-season plan. I don’t imagine a world where I would shift that plan. And, frankly, what we do in Season 3 doesn’t leave room for it."All 16 episodes of Paradise Seasons 1 and 2 are streaming exclusively on Hulu on Disney+.
